pr_title: Workaround the cache serialization bug on Ruby 3.2
pr_body:
Fix: https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/issues/23644

As mentioned on that other thread, the issue arise when a `Status` is created with SHAPE_TOO_COMPLEX making the instance variable ordering unpredictable.

But we can sidestep that issue using code inspired from Shopify/paquito.

I added some code in the test environment initializer to cause this issue to be reproduced and prove this change fixes it.

This code is also easily converted into a monkey patch.
pr_comments: Thank you for your work on this issue. I'm a magnet for these bugs, but sadly too dumb to fix them.

Thanks for the contribution!

I still need to actually review and test the `ActiveRecordCoder` part for soundness, but it looks good at a quick glance, and I ran a few benchmarks on a single local post with one parent and one reply:
- the payload stored in redis is about 47% smaller
- the serialization (including marshaling, compressing and storing to redis) is about 40% faster
- the deserialization (including fetching from redis, decompressing and unmarshaling) is about 52% faster

Very welcome change overall, I will try to do a full review very soon!

Also of note, there are other places where we serialize ActiveRecord objects, at least:
- `CustomFilter.cached_filters_for`
- `EntityCache`

I have not fully investigated them yet, but we should probably take care of that next, especially `EntityCache#status`.

1. deploy main at fb8503e861b630728ead4be847309f1fd7c03dd4
2. build docker image/deploy docker image
3. access mastodon 4.1.0 with 3.2.1
...




### Expected behaviour

business as usual

### Actual behaviour

Lots of errors in the mobile clients and web clients.

comments: I did `cache clear` and it didn't seem to help.

> access mastodon 4.1.0 with 3.2.1

I assume you mean `main`, as 4.1.0 does not support Ruby 3.2.

On main, I am unable to reproduce, even without `cache clear`. Is it possible you had both Ruby 3.2 and Ruby 3.0 workers running at the same time? Can you retry with `BACKTRACE=1` in your `.env.production`?
I don't believe so. I'm a little worried about running in production again, but I'll try to replicate this with BACKTRACE=1 in the next few days.

The errors were also seen when GETting the notification timeline. Puma and Sidekiq were on ruby-3.2.x with JIT disabled, on my server when the errors were recorded.

I'm running my test server using Ruby 3.2.1 and I really can't reproduce the issue.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/384364/220158617-dc9a5b41-f9a3-4d8a-a668-1f6cd3be8e6f.png)

It's when you `dup` and Active Record, the ivar order is different:

I'll have to consult with Aaron to see how we could control that ordering.

Ok, so the bad new is that once we fallback to `SHAPE_TOO_COMPLEX`, instance variables are held in an `id_table` which is an unordered map, so we have no way to control the order past this point.

I have to stop for the night, but a quick summary of what we discussed with Aaron:

We could change Ruby to use an `st_table`, which is ordered. Means waiting for `3.2.2`, and may increase memory usage sligthly (IMHO Ruby should do it regardless, but to be debated upstream).


We could defined `marshal_dump` and `marshal_load` in `ActiveRecord::Base`, this would allow us to control how the serialization happen. However the downside is that any payload generated from an app that has defined this can't be read by apps that din't. So it can cause deserialization during rolling restarts, which is a pain. That said `Marshal.dump(active_record)` is currently dumping way too many objects, so we should probably do this is Rails just for efficiency's sake.

We could try to make some changes in instance variables initialization order in both Rails and Mastodon to avoid hitting `SHAPE_TOO_COMPLEX`, but it's brittle and it's hard to guarantee the bug won't resurface.

I'll sleep on all this and see if I can come up with a decent fix, hopefully one that can be monkey patched. All this may take a tiny while, because one fix would be in Ruby, the other in Rails, so I can't just patch it willy nilly, I have to discuss with other committers first.
